hook_provenance.method: read-only inspection of the settings files (hook event / matcher / command kinds only) plus the auto-mode denial reproduced in this session; the interactive /hooks screen was not driven
hook_provenance.observation: A Bash call was rewritten by a PreToolUse hook (a grep pipeline became `rtk grep ...`) and auto mode refused it with `hook changed this call's input after auto mode reviewed it`; re-issuing the exact rewritten input once was accepted. The D7 log showed the same class (`git status` -> `rtk git status`). No setting was changed and no permission was bypassed.

agent.evidence: after D8 no .claude/agents/*.md declares `hooks`; pr_reviewer_guard.py never existed in this repository

user.evidence: the user-scope settings file registers a PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash whose command is the `rtk hook claude` rewriter (plus unrelated session / stop / notification hooks, not listed); permissions.defaultMode is auto

plugin.evidence: two plugins are enabled in user settings; their own hook registrations were not inspected

hook_provenance.conclusion: The input rewrite is attributed to the user-scope `rtk hook claude` PreToolUse hook (inferred from the registered command and the `rtk` prefix on the rewritten call; not independently traced). It is NOT evidence that the unmigrated pr_reviewer_guard.py ran.
hook_provenance.minimal_reproduction: In an auto-mode session with that user hook active, run any Bash command that rtk rewrites (for example `git status`); auto mode denies the call, and re-issuing the rewritten input is reviewed normally.
hook_provenance.not_done: user / global / plugin settings were not modified; auto mode was not bypassed; rtk was not removed
